questions.q: In a DDoS attack the large group of compromised computers controlled remotely by the attacker is called a
questions.exp: Bots under a command-and-control server form a botnet used to flood the victim.

questions.q: In an RSA system p = 3, q = 11 and e = 7. The ciphertext for plaintext m = 2 is
How many different passwords of exactly 3 lowercase letters (a-z, repetition allowed) are possible?
How does an Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) differ from an Intrusion Detection System (IDS)?
options: An IPS only works on hosts and an IDS only on networks
An IDS encrypts traffic and an IPS decrypts it
An IPS cannot detect attacks, it only logs them
An IPS sits inline and can actively block malicious traffic, whereas an IDS mainly alerts
questions.exp: IDS monitors and raises alerts; IPS is placed in the traffic path and drops or blocks attacks.

questions.q: Section 43A of the IT Act (inserted in 2008) deals with
options: Compensation when a body corporate fails to protect sensitive personal data
Cheating by personation using a computer resource
Publishing obscene material in electronic form
questions.exp: Section 43A makes a body corporate liable to pay compensation for negligence in protecting sensitive personal data.

questions.q: Compared with a differential backup, an incremental backup
options: Takes less time and space per run, but restoration needs more backup sets
Takes more space but restores from only two sets
Cannot be combined with a full backup
questions.exp: Incremental backups store only changes since the last backup of any kind, so a restore chains many sets.

questions.q: A free game installer secretly opens a backdoor on the computer but does not copy itself to other files or machines. It is a
questions.exp: A trojan masquerades as useful software and does not self-replicate.

questions.q: The default TCP port used by HTTPS is
questions.exp: HTTP uses 80, SSH 22 and SMTP 25; HTTPS (HTTP over TLS) uses 443.

questions.q: An ethical (white-hat) hacker differs from a malicious hacker mainly because the ethical hacker
options: Sells stolen data to the highest bidder
Attacks systems to promote a political cause
Tests systems with the owner's authorisation to find and report weaknesses
Writes malware to infect public computers
questions.exp: Authorisation and intent to improve security define ethical hacking.

questions.q: A hospital's patient records are secretly modified by an unauthorised person. Which principle of the CIA triad is violated?
questions.exp: Unauthorised modification of data violates integrity, which ensures data stays accurate and unaltered.

questions.q: In India, a patent is granted for a term of
options: 20 years from the date of filing
questions.exp: Under the Patents Act, 1970 the term is 20 years from the filing date.

questions.q: The main purpose of the TLS handshake is to
options: Compress the web page before transfer
Assign an IP address to the client
Authenticate the server and agree on cipher suite and session keys
questions.exp: The handshake verifies the server's certificate and establishes shared symmetric keys.

questions.q: Creative Commons licences are used to
options: Let creators grant specified permissions for others to share and reuse their work
questions.exp: CC licences are standard copyright licences that state what reuse is permitted.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of malware?
questions.exp: A honeypot is a decoy system used by defenders to study attackers.

questions.q: Alice wants to send Bob a confidential message using public-key cryptography. She should encrypt it with
questions.exp: Only Bob's private key can decrypt a message encrypted with his public key.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes AES?
questions.exp: AES (Rijndael) works on 128-bit blocks and supports key lengths of 128, 192 and 256 bits.

questions.q: The output size of the SHA-256 hash function is
questions.exp: SHA-256 yields a 256-bit digest (MD5 is 128 and SHA-1 is 160 bits).

questions.q: A login query is: SELECT * FROM users WHERE name='$u' AND pass='$p'. An attacker enters admin' -- as the username and anything as the password. What is the likely result?
options: The password check is commented out and the attacker logs in as admin
The server always returns a syntax error
The password is automatically hashed and compared
questions.exp: The quote closes the name string and -- starts a comment, so the AND pass condition is ignored.

questions.q: Which malware spreads across a network by copying itself, without needing a host file or any user action?
questions.exp: A worm is self-replicating and standalone; a virus needs a host file and a trojan does not replicate.

questions.q: An attacker sends a flood of TCP SYN packets and never completes the handshake, leaving the server with many half-open connections. This is a
questions.exp: A SYN flood exhausts the server's connection table with half-open connections, denying service to legitimate users.

questions.q: A DMZ (demilitarised zone) in network security is
options: A separate subnet exposing public-facing servers between the Internet and the internal network
A zone where all traffic is blocked permanently
A backup site in another city
A wireless network without a password
questions.exp: Placing web or mail servers in a DMZ limits damage to the internal LAN if they are compromised.

questions.q: In an RSA system n = 55 (p = 5, q = 11) and e = 3. The private exponent d is
In a stream cipher the plaintext bits 1011 are XORed with the key bits 0110. The ciphertext is
Withdrawing money from an ATM using a debit card and a PIN is an example of
options: Two factors, both of the 'something you know' type
Two-factor authentication (something you have plus something you know)
questions.exp: The card is something you have and the PIN is something you know, so two different factor categories are used.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT protected by copyright?
options: An idea or concept as such, apart from its expression
questions.exp: Copyright protects the expression of ideas, not ideas themselves.

questions.q: The number of rounds in AES when a 192-bit key is used is
questions.exp: AES uses 10, 12 and 14 rounds for 128, 192 and 256-bit keys respectively.

questions.q: In disaster recovery planning, a 'hot site' is
options: An empty building with only power and space
A fully equipped alternate facility with current data that can take over almost immediately
A vault that stores backup tapes
A site used only for printing records
questions.exp: Hot sites mirror systems and data for near-instant failover; cold sites are empty shells.

questions.q: An attacker forges the source IP address in packets so that they appear to come from a trusted host. This is
questions.exp: Spoofing falsifies the source address to impersonate another system.

questions.q: In India, a registered trade mark is initially valid for
questions.exp: Trade mark registration lasts 10 years and can be renewed indefinitely for further 10-year periods.

questions.q: The national nodal agency in India for responding to computer security incidents is
questions.exp: CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) handles cyber security incidents under the IT Act.

questions.q: Legal recognition to electronic records under the IT Act 2000 is given in Section
questions.exp: Section 4 gives legal recognition to electronic records, Section 2 holds definitions.

questions.q: Under the IT Act, certifying authorities are licensed and regulated by the
questions.exp: The CCA licenses CAs and supervises the issue of digital signature certificates.

questions.q: The rail fence cipher is an example of a
questions.exp: It rearranges letter positions in a zig-zag without changing the letters.

questions.q: An e-mail that appears to come from a bank asks the user to click a link and enter net-banking credentials on a look-alike page. This attack is called
questions.exp: Tricking users via deceptive messages into revealing credentials on fake sites is phishing.

questions.q: Malware that secretly records every key pressed by the user in order to steal passwords is
questions.exp: Keyloggers capture keystrokes and send them to the attacker.

questions.q: The primary purpose of a Virtual Private Network (VPN) is to
options: Increase the physical bandwidth of the link
Assign IP addresses dynamically to hosts
Create an encrypted tunnel for private communication over a public network
questions.exp: A VPN uses tunnelling and encryption so that data crossing the Internet stays confidential.

questions.q: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act was enacted in the year
questions.exp: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act received assent in August 2023.

questions.q: Under the IT Act 2000 (as amended in 2008), which section deals with punishment for identity theft?
questions.exp: Section 66C punishes fraudulent or dishonest use of another person's password, digital signature or unique identification feature.

questions.q: The '3-2-1' backup rule recommends
options: 3 copies of data, on 2 different media, with 1 copy kept off-site
3 full backups, 2 incremental backups and 1 differential backup
3 backups per day, 2 per week and 1 per month
questions.exp: Keeping three copies on two media types with one off-site guards against most failures.

questions.q: Every pair among 20 users must share a distinct secret key for symmetric encryption. How many keys are needed?
In a man-in-the-middle attack, the attacker
options: Secretly sits between two communicating parties and can read or alter their messages
Floods the server with traffic to make it unavailable
Encrypts the victim's files and demands money
Guesses passwords using a word list
questions.exp: MITM relays and possibly modifies communication while both ends believe they talk directly to each other.

questions.q: Files on a company server are renamed with a strange extension and a note demands payment in cryptocurrency for the decryption key. This malware is
questions.exp: Ransomware encrypts victim data and demands a ransom.

questions.q: In a fraud, a program deducts very small amounts such as fractions of a rupee from thousands of accounts and credits them to the attacker. This is a
questions.exp: Salami attacks slice off tiny amounts that individually go unnoticed.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a symmetric-key algorithm?
questions.exp: RSA is an asymmetric (public-key) algorithm; the others use one shared key.

questions.q: In disaster recovery, the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is
options: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time
The interval between two consecutive backups
The maximum acceptable time within which a service must be restored after a failure
The total cost of the backup system
questions.exp: RTO is about downtime; the data-loss tolerance is the Recovery Point Objective.

questions.q: A message DWWDFN was encrypted with a Caesar cipher using shift 3. The plaintext is
questions.exp: Shifting each letter back by 3: D→A, W→T, W→T, D→A, F→C, N→K.

questions.q: Copying the magnetic-stripe data of a debit card with a small device fitted on an ATM slot is called
questions.exp: Skimmers read card data (often with a hidden camera for the PIN) to clone cards.

questions.q: Authorisation differs from authentication in that authorisation
options: Verifies the identity of the user
Decides what an already identified user is permitted to do
questions.exp: Authentication proves who you are; authorisation grants permissions.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT plagiarism?
options: Submitting an essay written by someone else as one's own
Copying paragraphs from a website without acknowledgement
Quoting a passage in quotation marks with a proper citation of the source
Presenting another researcher's idea in your own words without crediting them
questions.exp: Properly quoted and cited material acknowledges the source; the others pass off others' work as one's own.

questions.q: The trail of data that a person leaves through online activities such as browsing, posting and purchasing is called the
questions.exp: A digital footprint is the data trail created by one's online activity.

questions.q: Which intrusion detection approach compares observed traffic with a database of known attack patterns?
questions.exp: Signature-based IDS matches events against stored patterns of known attacks; anomaly-based IDS looks for deviations from a baseline.

questions.q: A packet-filtering firewall makes its decisions mainly by examining
options: The full text of e-mail bodies
The physical condition of network cables
IP addresses and port numbers in packet headers
questions.exp: Packet filters inspect header fields such as source/destination IP address, port and protocol against rules.

questions.q: A zero-day attack is one that
options: Occurs on the day a computer is bought
Exploits a vulnerability unknown to the vendor for which no patch yet exists
Deletes all data in zero days
questions.exp: Defenders have had 'zero days' to prepare a fix.

questions.q: The main purpose of a CAPTCHA test on a website is to
options: Distinguish human users from automated bots
questions.exp: CAPTCHAs present challenges that are easy for humans but hard for bots.

questions.q: The most effective programming-level defence against SQL injection is
options: Making the input text boxes longer
Relying only on client-side JavaScript validation
questions.exp: Parameterised queries keep user data separate from SQL code, so input cannot alter the query structure.

questions.q: Under the Indian Copyright Act, 1957, copyright in a literary work generally lasts for
options: 20 years from the date of publication
questions.exp: For original literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works the term is the author's life plus 60 years.

questions.q: Cyber terrorism under Section 66F of the IT Act is punishable with
options: Imprisonment which may extend to life
questions.exp: Section 66F prescribes imprisonment that may extend to imprisonment for life.

questions.q: The science of analysing and breaking ciphers without knowing the key is called
questions.exp: Cryptanalysis attempts to recover plaintext or keys from ciphertext.

questions.q: A disgruntled employee's program deletes the payroll database if his name is removed from the payroll list. This is an example of a
questions.exp: A logic bomb stays dormant until a specific condition is met.

questions.q: Which section of the IT Act empowers the government to intercept, monitor or decrypt information in the interest of national security?
questions.exp: Section 69 authorises interception, monitoring and decryption of information through any computer resource under stated conditions.

questions.q: Which is the strongest sign that an e-mail link is a phishing attempt?
options: The e-mail arrived in the morning
The link's domain differs from the organisation it claims to represent
questions.exp: A mismatched or look-alike domain is a classic phishing indicator.

questions.q: A differential backup copies
options: Only files changed since the most recent backup of any type
All files changed since the last full backup
Only the files deleted since the last full backup
questions.exp: Differential backups grow each day because they always compare against the last full backup.

questions.q: Fraud carried out through voice calls in which a caller pretends to be a bank official to obtain OTPs is called
questions.exp: Vishing is voice phishing; smishing uses SMS.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT provided by a digital signature on its own?
questions.exp: A signature proves origin and integrity; the message stays readable unless it is also encrypted.

questions.q: An X.509 digital certificate essentially binds
options: A private key to a user's password
The identity of an entity to its public key, signed by a Certificate Authority
A user name to a MAC address
An IP address to a domain's TTL value
questions.exp: The CA signs the certificate to vouch that the public key belongs to the named subject.

questions.q: Users typing the correct URL of their bank are silently redirected to a fake site because DNS records were corrupted. This is
questions.exp: Pharming poisons DNS or host files to redirect users, even when they type the right address.

questions.q: A browser trusts a website's TLS certificate mainly because it
options: Is signed by a trusted CA whose root certificate is in the browser's trust store
questions.exp: Trust is chained from the site certificate up to a root CA that the browser already trusts.

questions.q: A full backup is taken every Sunday and an incremental backup every night from Monday to Saturday. The system fails on Thursday morning. How many backup sets are needed to restore it?
questions.exp: Restore requires the Sunday full plus incrementals of Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday: 1 + 3 = 4.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A hash value can be used to check the integrity of a downloaded file.
Reason (R): Any change in the file produces a different hash value.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Comparing the computed hash with the published hash reveals tampering because even a small change alters the hash.

questions.q: A toy hash function is h(x) = x mod 11. Which pair of inputs causes a collision?
questions.exp: 25 mod 11 = 3 and 36 mod 11 = 3, so both give the same hash; the other pairs give different values.

questions.q: Why is a random salt added to a password before hashing it?
options: To allow the password to be decrypted later
To defeat precomputed (rainbow table) attacks and make identical passwords hash differently
questions.exp: Per-user salts force attackers to attack each hash separately.

questions.q: Which practice is environmentally responsible for disposing of an old computer?
options: Handing it over to an authorised e-waste recycler
questions.exp: E-waste contains toxic materials such as lead and mercury and must be recycled through authorised channels.

questions.q: A company invents a new type of water-purification machine and wants exclusive rights over the invention. Which form of IPR applies?
questions.exp: Patents protect new, useful, non-obvious inventions.

questions.q: IPsec, commonly used to build VPNs, operates at which layer of the OSI/TCP-IP model?
questions.exp: IPsec secures IP packets themselves, so it works at the network layer.

questions.q: Using a Caesar cipher with key 3, the plaintext CAT is encrypted as
questions.exp: Each letter shifts 3 places forward: C→F, A→D, T→W.

questions.q: A list published by a Certificate Authority of certificates revoked before their expiry date is called a
questions.exp: Browsers can check the CRL (or use OCSP) to see whether a certificate is still valid.

questions.q: In a TLS session, after the handshake the bulk application data is encrypted using
questions.exp: Asymmetric methods establish the keys; fast symmetric encryption then protects the data.

questions.q:
Statement I: A stateful inspection firewall keeps track of the state of active connections.
Statement II: A firewall alone gives complete protection against attacks by trusted insiders.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.exp: Statement I is true; a firewall filters traffic at the perimeter and cannot stop all insider misuse, so Statement II is false.

questions.q: The main objective of the Information Technology Act, 2000 is to
options: Give legal recognition to electronic transactions and records and facilitate e-commerce and e-governance
Control the import of computer hardware
questions.exp: The Act provides legal recognition for electronic records and digital signatures and defines cyber offences.

questions.q: In Diffie-Hellman key exchange with p = 11 and g = 2, Alice's secret is 3 and Bob's secret is 4. The shared secret key is
questions.exp: A = 2³ mod 11 = 8; B = 2⁴ mod 11 = 5; key = 5³ mod 11 = 125 mod 11 = 4 (also 8⁴ mod 11 = 4).

questions.q: Which attack injects malicious client-side script into a web page that is later viewed by other users?
questions.exp: XSS makes the victim's browser execute attacker-supplied script from a trusted site.

questions.q: Which of the following is a passive attack?
questions.exp: Passive attacks only observe; replay, masquerade and DoS actively alter or disrupt communication.

questions.q: According to netiquette, typing an entire message in capital letters is generally regarded as
questions.exp: All capitals is read as shouting in online communication.

questions.q: Section 66A of the IT Act was struck down as unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in
options: Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)
questions.exp: In Shreya Singhal (2015) the Court held Section 66A violated freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a).

questions.q: A digital signature is created by encrypting the message digest with the
questions.exp: Only the sender holds the private key, so anyone can verify the signature with the sender's public key.

questions.q: A full backup is taken on Sunday and a differential backup each night from Monday to Saturday. The system fails on Friday morning. How many backup sets are needed to restore it?
questions.exp: Only the Sunday full backup and Thursday night's differential (all changes since Sunday) are needed.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of a firewall?
options: Repairing corrupted files on the hard disk
questions.exp: A firewall controls and logs network traffic; it does not repair files.

questions.q: Which kind of software is available free of cost but its source code is not made available?
questions.exp: Freeware costs nothing to use but remains proprietary with closed source.

questions.q: In a stored (persistent) XSS attack, the malicious script is
options: Saved on the target server, for example in a comment, and served to every visitor
Present only in a link sent to one victim
Stored on the attacker's USB drive
Executed only inside the database engine
questions.exp: Persistent XSS keeps the payload in server-side storage, so each viewer's browser runs it.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a property of a cryptographic hash function?
options: It must be possible to recover the original message from its hash
It produces a fixed-length output for any input size
It is hard to find two inputs with the same hash
A tiny change in input changes the output drastically
questions.exp: Hash functions are one-way; reversibility would defeat their purpose.

questions.q: Malware designed to hide its presence while keeping privileged access to a system is a
questions.exp: Rootkits conceal processes and files and give persistent administrator-level control.

questions.q: Match the attack with its description: (i) Smishing (ii) Whaling (iii) Spear phishing (iv) Pharming with (p) targets senior executives (q) fraudulent SMS (r) personalised e-mail aimed at a specific person (s) DNS redirection to a fake site.
questions.exp: Smishing uses SMS, whaling targets big fish such as executives, spear phishing is personalised and pharming redirects via DNS.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of the 'something you are' authentication factor?
questions.exp: Biometrics such as fingerprints are inherence factors.

questions.q: The principle of least privilege states that
options: Users and programs should get only the minimum access needed for their tasks
All users should have administrator rights
Passwords must be at least 8 characters
Data must be backed up weekly
questions.exp: Limiting rights reduces damage from errors or compromise.

questions.q: Backups run at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00. A failure occurs at 17:30 and the system is restored from the latest backup. How much data (in time) is lost?
questions.exp: The latest backup is at 12:00, so work from 12:00 to 17:30 = 5.5 hours is lost.

questions.q:
Statement I: In symmetric-key cryptography the same key is used for encryption and decryption.
Statement II: Asymmetric cryptography is generally faster than symmetric cryptography for bulk data.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.exp: Statement I is true. Public-key algorithms are far slower, so symmetric ciphers encrypt bulk data; Statement II is false.

questions.q: The DES algorithm processes 64-bit blocks using how many rounds?
questions.exp: DES is a 16-round Feistel cipher with a 56-bit effective key.

questions.q: For RSA with p = 7 and q = 11, which value of e is a valid public exponent?
questions.exp: φ(n) = 6×10 = 60. e must be coprime with 60; gcd(5,60)=5, gcd(6,60)=6, gcd(15,60)=15, but gcd(7,60)=1.

questions.q: Hiding a secret message in the least significant bits of an image file is called
questions.exp: Steganography conceals the existence of the message itself.

questions.q: Match the IT Act sections: (i) 66E (ii) 66F (iii) 67B (iv) 66D with (p) cyber terrorism (q) cheating by personation using a computer resource (r) child sexually explicit material (s) violation of privacy.
questions.exp: 66E is privacy violation, 66F cyber terrorism, 67B child pornography and 66D cheating by personation.
